source_text: In regions like parts of Europe and Asia with low routine circumcision rates, prevalence of diagnosed phimosis remains comparable (around 13-14% in some studies) but leads to fewer surgical referrals, favoring observation or non-invasive stretching over excision, reflecting views that the foreskin serves protective and sensory functions absent pathological evidence.
